full_name: Centre for the Governance of AI
mission: GovAI is a research organisation that studies how governments and AI companies should manage the arrival of very capable AI. It publishes policy research (regulation, compute, risk management, economics, security) and trains new AI-governance researchers through fellowships in London and Washington, DC.

key_work.title: Frontier AI Regulation: Managing Emerging Risks to Public Safety
key_work.plain_summary: An influential paper arguing that the most capable 'frontier' models need their own rules: safety standards, registration and reporting to government, and checks that companies follow them.

key_work.title: Computing Power and the Governance of Artificial Intelligence
key_work.plain_summary: Explains why AI chips and computing power are a practical 'handle' for governing AI: they are physical, countable and made by few firms, so governments can track and allocate them.

key_work.title: Coordinated Pausing: An Evaluation-Based Coordination Scheme for Frontier AI Developers
key_work.plain_summary: Proposes that when a lab's tests find a dangerous capability, all leading developers pause similar work together until the problem is understood.

key_work.title: Governing Through the Cloud
key_work.plain_summary: Describes how cloud compute providers could help regulators by securing AI systems, recording who trains big models, and enforcing rules.

key_work.title: Frontier AI Auditing: Toward Rigorous Third-Party Assessment of Safety and Security Practices at Leading AI Companies
key_work.plain_summary: Sets out how independent auditors could check AI companies' safety and security practices, rather than relying on companies grading themselves.

key_work.title: What If Automating AI R&D Triggers an Intelligence Explosion?
key_work.plain_summary: A multi-author paper (including Hinton and Bengio) on what happens if AI starts doing AI research itself: years of progress could be squeezed into months, straining oversight and control.

key_work.title: Embedded Assessments for Frontier AI
key_work.plain_summary: Argues for placing independent assessors inside AI companies so they can examine internal systems and practices that outside tests cannot see.

warnings.text: An 'intelligence explosion' from AI automating AI research could compress years of progress into months, creating urgent oversight and control problems.
Frontier models may develop dangerous capabilities (e.g. helping with biological or cyber attacks) that are hard to predict before release.
Voluntary company safety frameworks lack outside verification, so the public cannot tell whether they are followed.
Safety incidents may go unreported and unlearned-from without a formal incident-reporting regime.

recommendations.text: Regulate frontier AI specifically: safety standards, registration and reporting requirements, and enforcement.
Use compute (chips and cloud providers) as a lever for tracking and governing the largest training runs.
Require rigorous third-party audits and embedded assessments of AI companies' safety practices.
Build frontier-AI incident-reporting regimes so safety failures are found, investigated and shared.
